name: pdk-seaweedfs-replica-delete-convergence
instr:
SeaweedFS can leave deleted objects readable after a replicated volume server restarts: a delete reaches only currently registered holders, while a returning holder advertises its old bytes immediately. Fix replicated-volume deletion convergence in `/app` for replication `001` (two volume servers). A delete made while one holder is offline must leave its file ID pending until both copies are confirmed gone, including if the issuing filer restarts before the holder returns. The returning holder must catch up without relying on the issuing filer being alive, and must not serve stale bytes by direct HTTP GET or appear in master `/dir/lookup?volumeId=` or `LookupVolume` before catching up. Within 30 seconds of its return its live needle count (`/status` FileCount minus DeleteCount) must agree with the surviving holder, including when the issuing filer stays down for 45 seconds. If a holder stalls during a delete, the delete must complete within 25 seconds without waiting for it to resume, the surviving holder must clear its copy within 20 seconds while it is stalled, and the stalled holder must lose the deleted bytes within 10 seconds of resuming.

Keep normal S3 PUT, GET, DELETE and listings, filer metadata, direct volume reads, master lookups and replicated writes working. Deletes of 50 S3 objects during a 15–30 second holder outage must leave none of their file IDs readable on the returning holder from its first available `/status`.
